note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world - how many courts a venue has, whether it is indoor, when a session runs - come from the City of Tampa and are cited. Claims about our own coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Hillsborough County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. This is the second county in Florida this directory has published in, after Lee, and one city of it is on this page.

slots.coverage: One city in Hillsborough County is published here: Tampa, with sixteen venues and fifty-two courts verified against the City's own pickleball page, forty-five of them outdoors and seven inside community centres. Nothing else in the county has been read. Temple Terrace and Plant City are municipalities in Hillsborough with parks departments of their own, and the county government runs a parks department too, and none of those has been checked against a named source, so none appears anywhere on this site and this page does not characterise them - not their court counts, not whether they publish any. What this page reports is what the City of Tampa writes down: a count, an address and an indoor-or-outdoor label for every venue, hours for three outdoor venues, session schedules for every indoor one, and nothing about lighting, price or surface anywhere. Three venues inside Tampa itself are absent and named on the city page rather than dropped. Rowlett Park has eight courts, tied for the largest count in the city, at an address neither address resolver can find. Foster Park has two courts at an address the Census geocoder answers on the other side of the city and OpenStreetMap cannot find as written. The Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex has two indoor courts under two City house numbers, and the one that carries the count resolves to a postcode the City's own pages contradict. Each is one address away from being here, and between them they hold twelve courts.
slots.distribution: What is verified in this county is concentrated in one city and, within it, spread across sixteen sites rather than gathered into a complex. The largest published set is Macfarlane Park's eight outdoor courts; Cuscaden Park and Julian B Lane Riverfront Park hold six each, though Julian B Lane's six is "2 permanent courts" and "4 portable net courts" in the City's words; five venues hold four; the rest hold one or two. Forty-five of the fifty-two courts are outdoors on the City's label and seven are in community-centre buildings under its "Indoor Pickleball" heading - two each at Forest Hills and Loretta Ingraham, one each at Barksdale, Cordelia B Hunt and Port Tampa. That indoor seven is the county's distinctive number: Tampa has more published indoor venues than any city on this site, though Bellevue has more indoor courts, and it is one of the largest cities on the site where the operator states indoor or outdoor for every venue it publishes. The two halves are documented in opposite ways. The outdoor parks mostly carry a count and an address and nothing more - nine of twelve state no hours, and no venue in the county states lighting - while every indoor centre carries a session schedule, a phone number from the City's recreation-centres list, and in two cases a note that play resumes after summer camp. Forest Hills sits on both sides, two courts out and two in at one address, the second such venue on this site after Bellevue's Hidden Valley Park. Only one outdoor session is scheduled anywhere: Cuscaden Park's "Senior open play Wed 9-11 am".
slots.gaps: The honest position is that this is a Tampa page wearing the heading of a county, and the gap will not close by accident. Temple Terrace and Plant City have not been read; the county's own parks department has not been read; the threshold has not moved - three venues with a named source and a date - and nothing on this page says whether any of them would clear it. Inside Tampa the gaps are of two kinds. The first is the three refused venues, which are real places on the City's own list, twelve courts between them, absent for want of an address that resolves as the City writes it. Foster Park's is the instructive one: the Census geocoder answered "4700 S Clark Ave." with North Clark Avenue in a different postcode, which the street-type check built for Cape Coral could not see, so the resolver check was extended to catch a changed or dropped compass direction. That fix rescued Madison Street Park and Cordelia B Hunt, could not rescue Foster, and moved a published Bellevue venue to the street its City actually prints. The second kind of gap is silence inside published venues. The City states no lighting at sixteen venues, no price for fifty-two courts, no surface anywhere, and hours at only three outdoor sites; every indoor schedule carries dates with no year on a page dated 28 October 2025, and one court was "closed for repairs through June 1" of a June the City does not name. Nothing outside a municipal parks department appears here at all, and that absence is about who writes things down rather than where the game is played.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Hillsborough County?
faqs.a: We do not know, and no honest page can tell you. What we have checked is 52 courts across sixteen venues, all in Tampa, each with a source and a date you can see. The City of Tampa alone names three further venues with twelve courts that we cannot publish, and no other operator in the county has been read.

Because it is the only municipality in the county whose courts we have confirmed against a named source. A city appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source_url and a date_checked. Temple Terrace, Plant City and the county's own parks department have not been read, and this page says nothing about what they would show.

One page with a card for every venue. The City's pickleball page states a count and an address for each, labels every outdoor card "Outdoor Pickleball" and puts the community-centre courts under "Indoor Pickleball", so sixteen venues carry an indoor-or-outdoor answer in the City's own words. The recreation-centres page supplies the phone numbers.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Not stated. The City publishes no price for any court, and this site does not assume a park court is free. The one use of the word "free" on the City's page is "free beginner lessons" on Monday afternoons at the David M Barksdale Center, which prices a lesson rather than a court.

None that the City says. Not one of the sixteen cards mentions lighting, so every venue in the county is recorded as unverified, and there is no lights page for Tampa. The New Tampa Sports Pavilion prints hours to 9 pm, but the City does not write the word lights beside them.

In five City community centres: two courts each at Forest Hills and Loretta Ingraham, one each at Barksdale, Cordelia B Hunt and Port Tampa, all under the City's "Indoor Pickleball" heading and each with a session schedule. Port Tampa's card also says the court was closed for repairs through June 1.

faqs.q: How often is this checked again?
faqs.a: These pages were read on 7 September 2026, and every one of them is snapshotted into the repository that builds this site and re-asserted on every build. If the City changes a count, removes the Port Tampa repair note, or prints a resolvable address for Rowlett Park, the build fails and someone reads the page again.

sources.evidence: The sixteen published addresses matched at house-number level and were placed in Hillsborough County, FL (FIPS 12057), inside the incorporated place Tampa. Ten resolved through the Census address file as the City writes them and four through OpenStreetMap, two of those because the Census dropped or flipped a compass direction: "1224 E Madison St" came back "1224 MADISON ST", and "4602 N Himes Ave" came back "4602 S HIMES AVE, 33611". "2401 E Yukon St." (Rowlett Park) is found by neither resolver. "4700 S Clark Ave., 33611" (Foster Park) is answered by the Census as "4700 N CLARK AVE, 33614" and not found by OpenStreetMap. "220 N Oregon Ave." (Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex) resolves in 33606 against the City's 33607. Snapshot: data/sources/tampa-county-census.json
